summary: The comment discusses the impact of math apps on elementary students' learning and screen time, and advocates for tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes. The text discusses the impact of math apps and screen-based learning on students' educational experiences and attitudes. It highlights that students' views of math may change as a result of regular use of these apps, with some students shifting from viewing math as a problem-solving activity to seeing it as a game. The text emphasizes the importance of considering educational outcomes when evaluating the impact of E-Rate programs on students' learning environments. The text argues against using screen time as a condition for E-Rate eligibility, emphasizing the negative impact of screen time on learning and the development of children. It calls for urgent legislation to limit screen time for elementary-aged students to promote face-to-face learning experiences. The text cites the Student Mathematical Practices from the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM) as a key framework for teaching mathematics.
